title: Two-bar truss: bar force and joint deflection

source.work: Bentley Systems, STAAD.Pro Help, Verification Examples (public documentation, docs.bentley.com)
source.edition: STAAD.Pro Help v21 build (pages refer to the STAAD.Pro 2023 sample files), read 2026-11-22
source.notes: problem statement taken from the vendor page (text and input listing). The page cites: Timoshenko, Strength of Materials, Part I, 3rd ed. 1956, p. 10, problem 2 - NOT opened for this project; no number is taken from it. The page's 'theory' values are recorded as printed; the program's own results are not used.

analysis: Plane truss (X-Y plane, Y vertical; uz of every joint held): two bars of 180 in, each inclined 30 degrees to the horizontal, from two pinned supports down to a common joint; A = 0.5 in^2, E = 30e6 psi; 5000 lb downward at the joint. The page prints the bar stress; the target here is the bar force = stress x 0.5 in^2. Reference values: computed here from this statement (verification/derive/vendor_reference.py); the textbook cited by the vendor page was not opened and no number is taken from it.
